definition: In natural language processing, a topic model is a type of probabilistic, neural, or algebraic model for discovering the abstract topics that occur in a collection of documents.
details: Topic modeling is a frequently used text mining tool for discovering hidden semantic features and structures in a text. The topics produced by topic models are generated through a variety of mathematical frameworks, including probabilistic generative models, matrix factorization methods based on word co-occurrence, and clustering algorithms applied to semantic embeddings. Topic models are commonly used to organize and discover latent features in large collections of unstructured text and other forms of big data. Beyond text mining, topic models have also been used to uncover latent structures in fields such as genetic information, bioinformatics, computer vision, and social networks.

explainer.lead: A topic model is a probabilistic, neural or algebraic model for discovering the abstract topics in a document collection. It matters because it surfaces hidden semantic structure in large unstructured text.

tiers.eli5: It reads a big pile of documents and tells you the themes running through them, without being told what to look for.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use topic models for exploratory analysis and content organization across large corpora. A pitfall is treating the discovered topics as ground truth when they are statistical artifacts of the chosen framework.
tiers.paperLevel: Topics are produced through probabilistic generative models, matrix factorization on word co-occurrence, or clustering of semantic embeddings. Limits depend on the framework and data.

explainer.example: Running a topic model over support tickets reveals clusters such as billing issues and login problems.
